paras: The killing of Joe Walker took place at Skipwith, Mississippi, on the night of Saturday, December 9, 1882, when constable J. A. Lawson shot Walker, a Black man, while trying to arrest him for gambling. Walker died of the wound two days later, and Lawson was arrested and released on bail. The only account, a dispatch from Skipwith giving the constable's side, ran as a short crime item in papers from Mississippi to Minnesota.

According to the Skipwith dispatch, Lawson tried to arrest Walker, described as "colored," for gambling on Saturday night. The dispatch said Walker resisted and beat Lawson about the face and head, and that in the fight Lawson shot him in the stomach. Walker died of the wound on Monday, December 11. The papers do not say where in Skipwith the shooting happened or whether anyone else saw it.

Lawson was arrested and examined before Judge Root, with A. J. Wilkinson of Skipwith acting as his counsel. The Memphis Appeal reported that he was admitted to $500 bail "awaiting further testimony," while the St. Paul Daily Globe's copy of the same dispatch gave the bail as $5,000. No report of an inquest, grand jury action or trial appears in the coverage.

The story reached readers through one dispatch dated at Skipwith on December 11, which the Memphis Daily Appeal and the St. Paul Daily Globe printed nearly in full on December 12. A shorter Memphis version in the Washington National Republican ran under the headline "A Negro Gambler Killed," and the Globe titled its item "Shot His Man." On December 13 a one-sentence version appeared in crime roundups in the Daily Republican and the Lancaster Daily Intelligencer, the latter headed "Shot While Evading Arrest."

A week later the Brookhaven Ledger in Mississippi and the Weekly Chillicothe Crisis in Missouri carried brief notices, the Crisis writing that "the negro was shot and killed." Every version presented the constable's account, that Walker resisted and beat him, as fact and added no comment.

The two full texts of the dispatch differ on the bail, $500 in the Memphis Appeal and $5,000 in the St. Paul Globe. The National Republican's brief says Walker was "shot and killed" Saturday night, while the fuller reports say he lived until Monday.
